question.text: Who can be appointed as the Nodal Officer for IEPF-related matters in a company?

answer.text: Any employee designated by the Human Resources department
A Director, Chief Financial Officer, or Company Secretary of the company
The statutory auditor of the company
Any external consultant appointed by the Board of Directors

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook says the company shall nominate a Nodal Officer who shall be a Director, Chief Financial Officer, or Company Secretary, for the purposes of verification of claims and coordination with the IEPF Authority. Option B reflects that list directly. The Trap: Option A is too broad because the workbook restricts the Nodal Officer role to specific senior positions rather than any employee designated by HR. Option C (statutory auditor) and option D (external consultant) place the role outside the company's executive structure, which does not match the workbook's specified set of eligible officers. Note: The workbook also describes communication and display duties associated with the Nodal Officer role, which fits with the requirement that the position be held by a Director, CFO, or Company Secretary within the company rather than by an outside party.
